newsitem.title: UK: LME option declaration calm, copper upsides bought.
newsitem.headline: LME option declaration calm, copper upsides bought.

text.p: The LME options declaration went calmly on Wednesday as prices failed to challenge any strikes burdened with weighty open interest levels, traders said.
June copper was hovering just above $2,550 in the morning but by the declaration had edged about $5 below there, so $2,550 puts were declared.
Several dealers said $2,550 calls had been abandoned, but one said he had a partial declaration.
The straddling of $2,550 failed to cause jitters since open interest data from the LME showed only 145 lots of calls and 310 lots of puts at that strike.
"If prices had done about $20 more in the morning, people would have been nervous about the $2,600s like they were earlier in the week," one trader said.
Open interest in calls at $2,600 was 1,145 lots.
A new system inaugurated by the LME this month in which deep in-the-money options are automatically declared went without any hitches, traders said.
Despite the weakness in copper futures, which slipped to $2,462 basis three months by the end of the morning kerb, demand was still being seen for upside calls.
Traders reported buying this week, including Wednesday morning, of July and August calls at $2,600, $2,650 and $2,700, trading at 21.5 percent to 22.75 percent volatility.

"People are buying them as cheap protection...the market will have its correction, maybe down to $2,440 as the weak longs get out, but people still think it will go higher after that," one trader said.
Nearby at-the-money implied volatility was about one point firmer, with July bid at 20.0 to 21.0 percent and August bid at 17.75 to 19.0 percent. Fourth quarter was bid at 15.5 percent.
June aluminium moved little ahead of the declaration and ended around $1,568, so $1,550 calls and $1,575 puts were declared.
Open interest data showed 695 lots of $1,550 calls and 1,100 lots of $1,575 puts.
Aluminium volatility was little changed with July and August bid at 15.0 to 16.0 percent.
One trader said there had been some buying of July $1,575 and $1,600 calls on Monday and Tuesday.
Another said some two-way business had been seen in fourth quarter material, trading at 15.0 and 15.25 percent.
June zinc settled at $1,322, putting into play $1,300 calls, with 1,435 lots shown in open interest figures and $1,325 puts, with only 20 lots.
